vitoVip.title: Vito VIP Vehicle Service
vitoVip.description: Late-model Mercedes Vito with a private chauffeur. Comfortable travel for up to 6 passengers with luggage.
vitoVip.long: The Mercedes Vito is the vehicle our Middle Eastern guests choose most. It seats up to six people with their luggage in comfort, with generous legroom, tinted windows and separate air conditioning in the rear. You keep the same vehicle and the same driver for city sightseeing, airport pick-ups and intercity journeys.
features: Up to 6 passengers with luggage
Tinted windows for family privacy
Separate rear air conditioning
Free water on board, internet on request
Child seat on request
The same driver throughout your stay
vitoVip.long2: Let us be straight about capacity: with all six seats taken, the luggage compartment holds four large suitcases plus a few carry-ons. A family of seven, or a group travelling with two suitcases each, needs a second vehicle. We tell you this at booking, because discovering it at the airport is nobody's idea of a good surprise. Child and infant seats cost nothing extra, but they are not kept in the vehicle by default — they are fitted on request, so just tell us your child's age.
vitoVip.bestFor: Families travelling with luggage, groups of three to six, and long intercity journeys. If you are travelling alone or as a couple a smaller car will do, and we will say so ourselves.
vitoVip.how: The vehicle is priced by the job, not by the hour: airport transfers, full-day city use and intercity journeys are quoted separately. On a full-day booking the car and driver stay with you all day and wait between stops.
vitoVip.note: Child seats and extra luggage must be mentioned at booking. We do not offer self-drive rental; the vehicle always comes with its driver.

faq.question: How many suitcases fit with six passengers?
faq.answer: With six passengers the luggage compartment takes four large suitcases and a few carry-ons. If everyone is travelling with two suitcases we will suggest a second vehicle — tell us the number of people and bags at booking and we will confirm whether it fits before you arrive.

faq.question: Can I rent the vehicle without a driver?
faq.answer: No. The Vito comes with its driver only. Having someone who knows the city and speaks Arabic is the point of this service; for self-drive we will point you to a car rental company instead.

faq.question: Can I book the vehicle for a full day on my own itinerary?
faq.answer: Yes. On a full-day booking the car and driver stay with you all day, you decide where to go, and the driver waits at every stop. There is no obligation to follow a ready-made tour programme.

faq.question: Is it the same vehicle on intercity journeys?
faq.answer: Yes. Travelling to Bursa, Sapanca or anywhere else, neither the vehicle nor the driver changes. The driver who picked you up from your hotel is the one who brings you back, so you never have to explain your plans from scratch again.

sections.heading: How the price is set
sections.body:
There is no fixed rate card on the site, and that is deliberate. Three things set the price of a car with a driver: the distance, how many hours the car stays with you, and the date. Between a single airport-to-hotel run and a day that collects you in the morning and returns you in the evening the difference is four- or fivefold. Writing one number hides that difference.

So we give you the price while we talk: send your dates, how many you are and where you are going, and we send the total the same day. The figure we give does not change on arrival.

Included: fuel, parking, bridge and motorway tolls, and the driver's own costs. Nothing comes out of your pocket along the way. Not included: museum entry tickets, lunch and tips — and tipping is not obligatory; nobody will ask.

The charge is per job, not per hour. An airport pickup is one job; an eight-hour city tour is another. Which job we are talking about is clear from the start of the conversation.

sections.heading: What happens when the six seats are full
sections.body:
A Mercedes Vito carries six passengers. But the real question is not the seat count — it is whether passengers and luggage fit at the same time.

The honest arithmetic: with six people seated, the space behind takes two large suitcases and some hand luggage. A family of six arriving with six large cases does not fit in one Vito — and saying so at booking is better than discovering it at the airport.

In that case we send a second vehicle, and it comes from our own fleet. We do not take a booking and hand it to another company; the second car is the same model with the same team.

We do not have a single ten-seater, a minibus or a coach. Our fleet is built on one model and we are not changing that — the vehicle you see on the site is the one that meets you. For larger groups, two or three Vitos go out.

Child seats cost nothing extra but are not kept in the vehicle; you need to give the child's age at booking so it is fitted for that day.

sections.heading: A car for the day, or a one-way transfer
sections.body:
These are two different services, and confusing them leads to expecting the wrong price.

A one-way transfer is a single journey: airport to hotel, hotel to airport, or between two cities. The driver drops you and the job ends. If your arrival time is fixed and you do not need a car during the day, this is the right one.

With a car for the day, the vehicle and driver stay with you throughout. You get out where you like, look around and come back; the driver waits, parks and takes you to the next stop. On shopping days, when more than one district is being visited, or when travelling with a small child, the difference is large: you are not hunting for a car at every stop.

Which suits you usually comes down to this: more than two stops in the day means a car for the day; otherwise a one-way transfer makes more sense.

There is a third arrangement: intercity transfer. Going from Istanbul to Sapanca or Bursa and back the same day is not a one-way transfer but a full day's work.

sections.heading: What the driver does, and does not do
sections.body:
Our drivers speak Arabic, and that is what changes the whole journey. The hotel address, the luggage, a child seat, a request to stop — all of it is settled by talking rather than by gesture.

The driver knows the route, parks, waits and returns you to the hotel at the end of the day. He tells you about what you are passing and points you to restaurants and shopping. He fits prayer and meal breaks into the programme as you want them.

But a driver is not a licensed guide. In Türkiye, commentary inside museums and archaeological sites belongs to the licensed tourist-guiding profession, and a driver may not legally do it. On city tours an Arabic-speaking guide accompanies you; on some nature and shopping routes the Arabic-speaking driver takes on the guiding. We tell you plainly which applies to your programme before you book.

The same driver stays with you for the whole trip. You do not explain everything again each morning — with small children, the difference shows on the second day.

sections.heading: Which cities we cover
sections.body:
The car-with-driver service runs in six areas: Istanbul, Antalya, Bodrum, Trabzon, Bursa and Sapanca.

Airport meet-and-greet is available at five airports — Istanbul Airport (IST), Sabiha Gökçen (SAW), Antalya (AYT), Bodrum–Milas (BJV) and Trabzon (TZX). You are met at the arrivals gate with a name board; because we track the flight by its number, a delay simply moves the pickup and waiting is not charged.

Bursa and Sapanca do not count as separate areas: both are day trips from Istanbul and the car sets out from Istanbul. Bursa is two hours by ferry, Sapanca an hour and a half to two by road.

We also do intercity transfers, but only where the distance is reasonable. Istanbul to Trabzon is over a thousand kilometres and takes a full day each way by road; at that distance flying is the only sensible option, and we meet you on arrival.

sections.heading: What we put in writing before you book
sections.body:
The commonest complaint about car-with-driver services is a surprise charge. The only real protection against it is having everything in writing before the booking.

The message we send you contains: the total, how many hours the car stays with you, the route, the meeting point and time, and confirmation of a child seat if you asked for one. Those four or five lines close off almost everything that could be argued about later.

No extra charges appear along the way for parking, bridges or fuel. If you want to add a stop to the programme — which happens often — the driver relays it, and if there is a difference we say so at the time; it is not added to the bill afterwards.

We do not rent without a driver. The Vito goes out only with its driver; arriving with someone who knows the city and speaks Arabic is the point of this service. For guests who want to drive themselves there are car rental companies, and that is a different business.

transfer.title: Transfer & Meet and Greet
transfer.description: Airport pickup and hotel transfer at a fixed price, including flight tracking and luggage assistance.
transfer.long: For airport pick-ups we track your flight: if the plane is delayed the driver waits and there is no extra charge. Your driver meets you at the arrivals gate with a name board, handles your luggage and takes you straight to your hotel. Istanbul (IST), Sabiha Gokcen (SAW), Antalya (AYT), Bodrum (BJV) and Trabzon (TZX) airports are covered.
features: Flight tracking — waiting on delays is free
Name-board meet and greet at arrivals
Five airports: IST · SAW · AYT · BJV · TZX
Fixed price, confirmed at booking
Discount on round-trip bookings
Extra stops can be added
transfer.long2: At Istanbul Airport the meet-and-greet happens in international arrivals, directly opposite the exit doors, where your driver waits with a name board. At Sabiha Gökçen the arrivals hall is smaller and there is a single meeting point, so there is no room for confusion. Passport queues can run long at peak hours; the driver waits for you to come out, not for the plane to land, and we do not charge for that time. If your luggage is delayed or missing, one line on WhatsApp is enough.
transfer.bestFor: First-time visitors to Türkiye, flights landing at night, and families with small children. Anyone who would rather not queue for a taxi or haggle over the fare.
transfer.how: At booking we take your flight number, landing time and hotel address. We track the flight until arrival day and send the driver according to the new time. The price is per vehicle, fixed at booking, with nothing added on arrival.
transfer.note: We cannot track a flight without its number, so we always ask for it at booking. If your hotel changes later, a WhatsApp message is enough and there is no extra charge.

faq.question: Where exactly will I find the driver at the airport?
faq.answer: At Istanbul Airport he waits in international arrivals, opposite the doors you come through after baggage claim, holding a board with your name. At Sabiha Gökçen there is a single arrivals hall and a single meeting point. Your driver's name and phone number reach you on WhatsApp before your flight.

faq.question: How long is the journey from the airport to the hotel?
faq.answer: From Istanbul Airport to the Taksim and Sultanahmet area takes roughly 45-70 minutes depending on traffic. From Sabiha Gökçen to the European side takes 60-90 minutes. These are approximate; bridge traffic in the evening can stretch them.

faq.question: Do you meet flights that land after midnight?
faq.answer: Yes, there is no time limit. A flight landing at three in the morning is met with the same name board. We do not apply a night surcharge; the price is the same as during the day.

faq.question: What information do you need to make a booking?
faq.answer: Flight number, landing date and time, hotel name or address, number of passengers and number of suitcases. If you are travelling with children, add their ages so we can fit the right seat. With those five details a booking takes minutes.

transfer.metaDescription: Meet and greet and hotel transfer from Istanbul Airport (IST) and Sabiha Gökçen (SAW). Fixed price, flight tracking, a name board at arrivals, luggage help.

sections.heading: What happens after the plane lands
sections.body:
The most misunderstood part of an airport pickup is assuming the landing time and the time you walk out are the same. The gap between them is missing from most plans.

The real sequence: the plane lands, docks at the gate, passport control can reach twenty minutes at busy hours, and another fifteen to twenty minutes pass before the luggage reaches the belt. So you are at the exit about forty minutes after landing; an hour at a busy time.

That wait is our problem, not yours. Because we track the flight by its number, the driver is there before you and waiting is not charged. If your luggage goes missing and you are delayed, the driver waits too.

The meeting point is the arrivals gate and the driver waits with a board carrying your name. So it does not matter if you have no internet — if your line is not active yet or you cannot reach the wifi, the pickup still works.

sections.heading: Which airport, which district, how long
sections.body:
Istanbul has two airports, and which one you land at changes the distance to your hotel entirely.

Istanbul Airport (IST) is in the north-west of the city. To Taksim and Şişli it is about 40 kilometres: 45 minutes with clear roads, an hour and a half in the late afternoon. Sultanahmet is 45 kilometres and similar. Beşiktaş and Ortaköy are 42 kilometres.

Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) is on the Asian side, near Pendik. Asian-side districts such as Kadıköy and Ataşehir are reached in half an hour with no bridge crossing at all. But if your hotel is in Sultanahmet, Taksim or Beşiktaş you must cross a bridge, and the drive can stretch to an hour and a half or two.

In the other cities: Antalya Airport (AYT) lies east of the city — Belek 30–45 minutes, Side about an hour, Kemer 50 minutes to 1.5 hours, Alanya 1.5–2.5 hours. Bodrum–Milas (BJV) is about 36 kilometres and 40 minutes from the centre. Trabzon Airport (TZX) is inside the city, fifteen minutes from the middle.

Because we take the full hotel name at booking, we can give the real time rather than an estimate; two hotels inside the same area name can be twenty minutes apart.

sections.heading: Night arrivals and early-morning flights
sections.body:
A large share of flights from the Gulf land after midnight, and that is when public transport is at its weakest.

Nothing changes for a night arrival: the driver is at the arrivals gate as usual, with the name board as usual. We charge nothing for the hour and we have no line item called a night tariff.

On early-morning flights the real question is not traffic but what time you leave the hotel. If you need to be at the airport three hours before departure and the drive is forty-five minutes, we work out the departure time with you. Morning traffic in Istanbul thickens after half past six; leaving an hour early usually beats waiting an hour.

When you give us your flight number we track the return the same way. If the departure time changes we move the booking to the new time at no extra charge.

sections.heading: Luggage, child seats and larger families
sections.body:
A Mercedes Vito carries six passengers, but seats and luggage fitting at the same time is a separate sum. With six people seated, the space behind takes two large suitcases and some hand luggage.

If you are six with six large cases, a second vehicle is needed, and it comes from our own fleet. Saying so at booking beats finding out at the airport — which is why we ask how many suitcases there are.

Child and infant seats cost nothing extra but are not kept in the vehicle; you need to give the child's age at booking so one is fitted for that day. A pushchair goes in the boot and counts in the space calculation.

If you are travelling with a wheelchair, or an older relative who finds walking difficult, write that too: we set the meeting point and where the car pulls up around it.

tours.title: Guided Tours
tours.description: Daily tours and private tour programs with an Arabic-speaking guide.
tours.long: Our tours are private; you never join a group of strangers. The programme flexes around your sleeping and eating times, with stops at prayer times. Your guide speaks Arabic and explains each place in your own language. We have ready-made programmes for Istanbul, Bursa, Sapanca, Trabzon and Bodrum, and we can build a route around what you want to see.

Arabic-speaking guide or driver
Prayer and meal breaks built in
Hotel pick-up and drop-off
Relaxed pace for families with children
Custom routes on request
tours.long2: A tour day runs like this: the driver waits outside your hotel, you set off for the first stop, the route pauses at prayer times at mosques along the way, and lunch happens at a restaurant with halal options. The order of stops can shift with weather and traffic, but the number of stops does not. Museum and heritage site entrance fees are not included, because they vary from person to person; we tell you in writing before booking roughly what is payable at each stop.
tours.bestFor: Families who want to travel at their own pace, first-time visitors who would rather not struggle with the language, and couples who do not want to be folded into a large group.
tours.how: You are collected from your hotel and returned there at the end of the day. Pick a ready-made programme from the list, or we build one from scratch around what you want to see. The price is per vehicle, not per person; two people or six, the vehicle price is the same.
tours.note: Museum entrance fees and lunch are not included in the price. Cancellations made up to 24 hours before the programme starts are free of charge.

faq.question: Are museum entrance fees included in the price?
faq.answer: No. Museum and palace entrance fees change with the number of visitors, their ages and that year's tariff, so we leave them out of the price. Rather than hide that, we share in writing before booking roughly what is payable at each stop — and we can buy the tickets on your behalf if you prefer.

faq.question: Can I change a ready-made tour to suit me?
faq.answer: Yes. The ready-made programmes are a starting point; you can drop a stop, add one, or reorder the day. We can also build a route entirely around you — write down the places you want to see and we will plan the day.

faq.question: Is there a guide on the tour, or only a driver?
faq.answer: City tours are accompanied by an Arabic-speaking guide who explains the history of each place. On some nature and shopping routes the Arabic-speaking driver takes on the guiding instead. We tell you plainly which applies to your programme before you book.

faq.question: What is the minimum group size for a tour?
faq.answer: One person. Because our tours are private there is no minimum, and you never wait for a group to fill up. Since the price is per vehicle, the more of you travel together, the less each person pays.

sections.heading: The difference between a private tour and joining a group
sections.body:
Most day-tour sellers in Türkiye lower the price by putting you in a group: a coach of fifteen to twenty people, a fixed route and one timetable everyone must keep. That is why it is cheap.

On our tours the vehicle is yours alone. We collect you from the hotel and return you there; nobody else gets in along the way. The trade-off is plain: per person a private tour costs more, but with families of more than three the gap closes, because the price is per car.

What changes in practice is flexibility. On a group tour you get twenty minutes at a stop and the coach leaves. On a private tour you can stay forty, or leave after ten if you have had enough. Travelling with a small child or an elderly relative, that difference becomes the holiday itself.

Let us say it plainly: we are not the right address for a traveller looking for the cheapest. We do not cut the price by merging groups, and we write that here rather than disappoint you later.

sections.heading: The rhythm of the day: prayer, meals and children
sections.body:
The programme is built around how Gulf families run their day, not around a coach timetable.

The departure time is yours. A family that breakfasts late can leave at ten; someone who wants to be out before the heat leaves at eight. A group tour offers no such choice.

Breaks are taken at prayer times and the driver knows the nearest mosque. You choose where to stop for lunch; if there is any doubt about halal, the driver asks, so you do not have to.

With children we apply the rule of two main stops a day. A third fits on paper, but the child tires and the evening goes with it. If you want to return to the hotel mid-day and rest for two hours, that is possible too — the car is yours and so is the plan.

If you have a pushchair, a wheelchair or an older relative who finds walking hard, the stops are chosen around that: the cobbled lanes of the historic peninsula are not the same as the seafront.

sections.heading: What the price includes and what it does not
sections.body:
The tour price is per vehicle and is fixed at booking; it does not change on arrival.

Included: the private car and driver, hotel pick-up and drop-off, fuel, parking and tolls, water in the vehicle, and an Arabic-speaking guide on city tours.

Not included: museum and archaeological site entry tickets, lunch, boat-trip tickets and tips. We keep museum tickets out of the price because the fees change and because not everyone visits the same museums — we would rather the choice stayed yours.

Tipping is not obligatory and nobody will ask. It is a common habit in Türkiye but not an expectation; you tip if you were pleased.

If you want to add a stop to the programme the driver relays it; if there is a difference we say so at the time, and it is not added to the bill afterwards.

sections.heading: Guide or driver, and on which tour
sections.body:
We write this distinction out because the two are not the same, and confusing them skews expectations.

On city tours an Arabic-speaking guide accompanies you and explains the history of what you visit. In Türkiye, commentary inside museums and archaeological sites belongs to the licensed tourist-guiding profession; a driver may not legally do it.

On some nature and shopping routes the Arabic-speaking driver takes on the guiding instead. There is no museum to interpret on the shore of Lake Sapanca or in the Grand Bazaar; what helps there is someone who knows the way and speaks your language.

We tell you which applies to your programme before you book. You do not need to ask — it is written into the quote.

When choosing a hotel we tell you in advance how family-friendly it is, how close it is to the centre and the metro, and whether breakfast is included. flightHotel.long2: When we suggest a hotel we tell you two things up front: what the surrounding neighbourhood is actually like, and how many minutes on foot it is to the metro and tram. Staying in Sultanahmet lets you walk the historic peninsula but the evenings are quiet; Taksim and Şişli are livelier but the traffic is heavier. We explain those differences before you book. On flights we ask how flexible your dates are — flying a day earlier or later often makes a real difference.
flightHotel.bestFor: Travellers who want the ticket, the hotel, the transfer and the tour arranged in one place, and guests who cannot decide which district to stay in and would rather not read Turkish websites.
flightHotel.how: You send your dates, party size and budget on WhatsApp; two or three options come back with the total price for each. You approve the one you like and we make the booking. Ticket, hotel, transfer and tour all move through the same conversation.
flightHotel.note: We do not handle visa applications. Change and cancellation terms on a flight ticket follow the airline's own rules, and we put those in writing before the ticket is bought.

faq.question: Do you charge an extra service fee for bookings?
faq.answer: You pay the total price we quote you, and nothing more. No separate service charge is added after booking, and we start no process until you have approved the price.

faq.question: Do you help with visa applications?
faq.answer: No, we do not handle visa applications. Visa rules differ by country and passport and change often; we would rather tell you this is not something we do than give you wrong information. You need to apply through the Turkish consulate in your own country or the official e-Visa site.

faq.question: Which hotels do you recommend?
faq.answer: The hotels page on our site lists notable hotels across four main districts of Istanbul, neighbourhood by neighbourhood. It is not a list of partner hotels — it is a map to help you decide where to stay. We can book the hotel you choose on your behalf.

faq.question: Can I change my flight ticket later?
faq.answer: Changes and cancellations depend on the airline's rules and your fare class. Some tickets can be changed, others are entirely non-refundable. We tell you in writing what is possible in your fare class before the ticket is bought.

sections.heading: Why let us handle the booking
sections.body:
You can book the hotel yourself, and we say so plainly. A booking made through Booking.com or the hotel's own site usually goes through without trouble.

The one sensible reason to ask us is knowing the district and asking the right questions. We ask what the listing does not say — which floor the room is on, what the window faces, whether the bathroom has a bidet spray, whether a family room is genuinely one room or two adjoining, whether an extra bed is charged.

We have no list of partner hotels and we add no commission to the price. So we have no interest in steering you to a particular one; when we say which hotel suits you, we are not looking at our own pocket.

We pass on the hotel's answer as it is. If the hotel is unsure, we say "unsure"; we do not present our guess as the hotel's word.

sections.heading: The questions we ask when choosing a hotel
sections.body:
Before suggesting a hotel we ask you three things: how many you are and the children's ages, which airport you land at, and whether you want to explore or to rest. Those three settle the district on their own.

The district decision comes before the hotel, because the wrong district in Istanbul means an hour and a half of travel a day. Over a five-day holiday that is a full day. A guest in Sultanahmet walks out of the hotel to Hagia Sophia; a guest in Şişli sets out every day to see the same thing.

Then we check the hotel's address on a map. In Türkiye a hotel may freely use a district name: one with "Taksim" in its name can be a twenty-minute walk uphill from the square. It is the complaint that recurs most in reviews.

Finally we read the last six months of reviews rather than the star rating. Stars measure a property's facilities — rooms, lifts, pool — not the quality of service.

sections.heading: Flights: what we do and what we do not
sections.body:
We buy the ticket in your name and send the details in writing. On domestic connections we plan the arrival time together with the transfer — that is the commonest problem when the ticket and the pickup are arranged separately.

Change and cancellation terms follow the airline's own rules and the fare class; we impose none of our own. Some tickets can be changed, some are never refundable. We tell you in writing before buying which class it is and what the terms are, so nothing is learned afterwards.

We do not handle visa applications. Visa rules vary by nationality and change often; we would rather not do the work at all than give you wrong information.

The ticket price is not part of the programme. In our packages the flight is a separate line, and we buy it in your name if you want or you buy it yourself — either is fine.

sections.heading: How payment and confirmation work
sections.body:
Before booking we send the total in writing: hotel name, room type, dates, how many people, whether breakfast is included. Those lines close off most of what could be argued about later.

The booking is made in your name, not ours. You are the one who arrives at the hotel and your name is the one at reception; you are not left depending on a middleman.

If a problem comes up, we hold the correspondence: room type, dates and confirmation. We deal with the hotel, so you are not left arguing at reception.

Contact runs through WhatsApp and everything stays written down. A confirmation given verbally on the phone is a confirmation nobody remembers later.

tours.title: Tour Destinations
tours.subtitle: Guided tours in Türkiye's most loved cities

istanbul.name: Istanbul Tour
istanbul.description: Blue Mosque, Hagia Sophia, Grand Bazaar and a Bosphorus cruise.
istanbul.long: The Istanbul tour lets you see a city spread across two continents in a single day. It starts in Sultanahmet Square, where the Blue Mosque, Hagia Sophia and Topkapi Palace are all within walking distance. The afternoon leaves time for the Grand Bazaar and the Spice Bazaar, and the day closes with a Bosphorus boat trip.
istanbul.season: April–May and September–October. In midsummer the middle of the day is hot and crowded, so the programme spreads across early morning and late afternoon.
istanbul.pace: Around 3–4 km of walking across the day. Topkapi Palace itself is a large site; you spend an hour or two on your feet inside.
istanbul.tip: In mosques shoulders and knees must be covered and women need a headscarf; a free cover is provided at the entrance. Shoes come off, so socks help.
istanbul.metaDescription: Blue Mosque, Hagia Sophia, Topkapı, the Grand Bazaar and a Bosphorus cruise in one day. Private vehicle, Arabic-speaking guide, hotel pick-up, never a group.
istanbul.metaTitle: Istanbul Tour — 8 Hours, Private Car and Guide

bursa.name: Bursa Tour
bursa.description: Uludağ cable car, Grand Mosque and Cumalıkızık village.
bursa.long: Bursa was the first Ottoman capital and is the greenest city within a day trip of Istanbul. After the ferry crossing you ride the cable car up Mount Uludag, then visit the Grand Mosque, the Green Tomb and the silk market at Koza Han. The day ends in Cumalikizik, a UNESCO-listed Ottoman village.
bursa.season: December–March for snow, April–June for greenery. The cable car can close in bad weather.
bursa.pace: Moderate walking in town; the stone lanes of Cumalikizik are narrow and sloping, so comfortable shoes matter.
bursa.tip: At the summit of Uludag it is 8–10 degrees colder than the city; even in summer bring a light jacket.
bursa.metaDescription: Uludağ cable car, the Grand Mosque, Koza Han and Cumalıkızık village. A day trip from Istanbul by ferry with a private vehicle, guide and hotel pick-up.
bursa.metaTitle: Bursa and Uludağ Tour from Istanbul — 10 Hours

sapanca.name: Sapanca Tour
sapanca.description: Lake Sapanca, Maşukiye waterfalls and nature walks.
sapanca.long: Sapanca and Masukiye are the closest green escape to Istanbul. The day centres on lakeside walks, waterfalls in the forest and trout restaurants built over the streams. A stop at Kartepe gives you the view down over Lake Sapanca. A calm, unhurried programme that suits families with children.
sapanca.season: April–October is the easiest window. In winter people go to Kartepe for snow, but road conditions vary.
sapanca.pace: The calmest programme on the site; walking is limited and optional. The best tour for families with children and older guests.
sapanca.tip: Paths around the waterfalls can be unpaved and wet; a pushchair will not roll easily everywhere.
sapanca.metaDescription: Lake Sapanca, the Maşukiye waterfalls and trout restaurants. 130 km from Istanbul as a day programme; collected from your hotel and returned by evening.

trabzon.name: Trabzon Tour
trabzon.description: Uzungöl, Sumela Monastery and the Black Sea highlands.
trabzon.long: A full-day programme combining the green highlands of the Black Sea with the history of Trabzon. The two main stops are Sumela Monastery, carved into a cliff face, and the lakeside village of Uzungol. Along the way there are stops at the Zigana pass, tea gardens and Hamsikoy for its rice pudding.
trabzon.season: Late June–September for the plateaus. Some plateau roads close in winter; Uzungol is open year-round.
trabzon.pace: A long drive with little walking. The climb to the Sumela Monastery is steep and not suitable for every age.
trabzon.tip: The Black Sea is Türkiye's rainiest region; a raincoat helps even in summer and mist can close the view.
trabzon.metaDescription: Uzungöl, Sumela Monastery and the Black Sea highlands with a private vehicle and Arabic-speaking guide. Highland season, distances and days needed explained.

bodrum.name: Bodrum Tour
bodrum.description: Bodrum Castle, turquoise bays and boat trips.
bodrum.long: The Bodrum tour combines ancient history with Aegean bays in one day. You start at Bodrum Castle and the Museum of Underwater Archaeology, then take in the town and harbour from the Ancient Theatre. The day continues with a boat trip around the bays and swimming stops, ending with free time at Yalikavak Marina.
highlights: Bodrum Castle and underwater archaeology museum
bodrum.season: May–October. The sea is warmest between July and September; April and November are cooler but quiet.
bodrum.pace: No walking on the boat trip; moderate around the castle and bazaar. Sun protection is needed.
bodrum.tip: Boat trips include a swimming stop, so bring swimwear and a towel. The midday Aegean sun is strong; a hat helps.
bodrum.metaDescription: Bodrum Castle, turquoise bays and an Aegean boat trip. Private vehicle and Arabic-speaking guide, hotel pick-up, and a day that flexes around your plans.
bodrum.metaTitle: Bodrum and Aegean Bays Tour — 10 Hours

antalya.name: Antalya Tour
antalya.description: Kaleiçi, the Düden Waterfall and Mediterranean bays.
antalya.long: The Antalya tour brings the history and the sea of the Mediterranean coast together in a single day. It starts in Kaleiçi: Hadrian's Gate from the Roman period, narrow stone lanes, Ottoman houses and gulet boats moored in the old harbour. In the afternoon you move on to the point where the Düden Waterfall falls into the sea, then free time on Konyaaltı or Lara beach. The day closes with shopping in the Kaleiçi bazaar and a walk around the harbour in the evening.
highlights: The old harbour and its gulets
Free time in the Kaleiçi bazaar
antalya.season: April to November. The sea is warm from May to October; July and August are very hot, so the programme spreads to early morning and late afternoon. In winter the city is quiet and green.
antalya.pace: Two to three kilometres of walking in Kaleiçi, on cobbled and sometimes sloping lanes. The waterfall walk is short. A pushchair is hard work in Kaleiçi.
antalya.tip: There is little shade; bring a hat, sunscreen and water. In swimming season bring swimwear — we stop at the beach. Haggling works in the Kaleiçi lanes.
antalya.metaDescription: Kaleici, Hadrian's Gate, the Duden Waterfall and Mediterranean beaches in one day. Private vehicle, Arabic-speaking guide and hotel pick-up.

about.title: About Us
about.subtitle: Rufai Tourism — Turkish expertise, Arabic hospitality
about.p1: We are a travel agency based in Türkiye, serving guests from the Middle East. Private transfers, guided tours, flight tickets and hotel bookings all come from one place.
about.p2: Our team speaks Arabic, Turkish and English, and stays with you from the moment you land until your departure. Our prices are fixed and agreed in advance — no surprise charges.
about.p3: We pay particular attention to family comfort: spacious vehicles, full privacy, and flexible schedules that respect prayer and rest times.
about.p4: The way we work is simple: every guest has a single point of contact. The team that meets you at the airport is the team that drives you around the city, so you never have to explain yourself twice.
about.p5: We are direct about price. You get the total in writing before you book, and no charges appear later for parking, bridges or fuel. Surprise fees are the fastest way to lose trust in this business.
about.p6: We build our programmes around the habits of Gulf families: a late breakfast, stops at prayer times, a pace that works for children and a private vehicle that protects your privacy. You never join a group tour; the day is yours.
about.proofSubtitle: Promises are easy. What follows are things you can verify yourself.
about.proof1Title: We have a physical office in Istanbul
about.proof1Desc: We are not a virtual address or a broker working by phone alone. We have an office with a sign in Istanbul and our own yard where the vehicles are parked. The photographs on this site are not stock images — they are of that office and those vehicles.
about.proof2Title: The vehicles are our own fleet
about.proof2Desc: We do not take your booking and hand the work to someone else. Every vehicle in the fleet is the same model of black Mercedes Vito, and we operate all of them ourselves. When a second vehicle goes out for a larger family, it is not hired in from outside.
about.proof3Title: The TÜRSAB record can be verified
about.proof3Desc: Our licence number is 12539. Operating as a travel agency without a licence is prohibited in Türkiye, so the licence means we work under the supervision of the Ministry of Culture and Tourism. You do not have to take our word for it — you can see the record yourself on TÜRSAB's official agency search page.
about.proof4Title: We are not right for everyone
about.proof4Desc: If you are looking for the cheapest option, we are not the right address: we work with a private vehicle, a chauffeur and a fixed price, and we do not lower the price by folding you into a group. Saying so up front beats disappointing you later.
about.wrongTitle: What happens when something goes wrong
about.wrongSubtitle: On every trip something does not go to plan. What matters is what happens then — so we write it down here.
about.wrong1Title: Your flight is delayed or cancelled
about.wrong1Desc: We track the flight by its number; the driver comes at the new time and waiting is not charged. If the flight is cancelled outright, just message us and we rebuild the transfer around the new date.
about.wrong2Title: Something goes wrong with the vehicle
about.wrong2Desc: The fleet is ours; we do not take a booking and hand it to another company. A replacement comes from the same fleet, so there is no waiting for “the other firm to send someone”. You write to one number.
about.wrong3Title: A problem comes up at the hotel
about.wrong3Desc: If we made the booking in your name, we hold the correspondence: room type, dates and confirmation. We deal with the hotel, so you are not left arguing at reception.
about.wrong4Desc: Our tours are private; you are not tied to a group. The day can be paused, shortened or moved to tomorrow — nobody is kept waiting for that. Going back to the hotel early is an option too.
about.wrong5Desc: Say it during the trip, not after. What is said the same day can be fixed; what is said after you fly home is only a review. We would rather hear the complaint.
about.wrongNote: The money side — cancellation, refunds and changes — is agreed in writing at booking and sent with the quote. We do not put a blanket sentence here because it varies by service and by date.

contact.prepSubtitle: Whether we can send a fixed price and a draft programme the same day comes down to these six lines. Without them we have to ask first, and a day is lost.
contact.prep1Desc: Arrival and departure. Prices move with the season and availability depends on the date — a figure given without dates is a guess.

contact.prep4Desc: The full hotel name if it is booked, otherwise the district you have in mind. Two districts from the same airport can differ by half an hour.
contact.prep5Desc: A transfer only, a single day tour, or a day-by-day programme. If you want hotels and flights arranged too, say so.
contact.prep6Desc: Extra suitcases, a pushchair, a wheelchair, or an older relative who finds walking difficult. These change the vehicle and the plan.
contact.prepNote: If you do not know all of it, write anyway — we start with what you have and fill in the rest together. We reply in Arabic, Turkish or English.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: What our guests ask most
faq.q1: Are prices fixed or do they change?
faq.a1: Published prices are fixed and confirmed before booking. There are no extra fees or surprises on arrival.
faq.a2: Yes, all our tours are accompanied by a fluent Arabic-speaking guide or driver.
faq.q3: How many passengers fit in a Vito?
faq.a3: The Mercedes Vito comfortably seats up to 6 passengers with luggage. For larger families we arrange more than one vehicle.
faq.q4: Do you meet us at the airport?
faq.a4: Yes. We track your flight, meet you at the arrivals gate with a name sign, and help with your luggage.
faq.q5: How do booking and payment work?
faq.a5: Booking takes minutes over WhatsApp. We agree on the program and price; you can pay on arrival or in advance, as you prefer.
faq.q6: Are the tours private or do we join a group?
faq.a6: Every tour we run is private. You are never merged with a group you do not know; the vehicle, the driver and the programme are yours alone. That is why prices are quoted per vehicle rather than per person.
faq.q7: What happens to the pick-up if my flight is delayed?
faq.a7: We track your flight. If it is delayed the driver comes at the new time and we do not charge for waiting. If you are held up at baggage claim, the driver waits for you there too.
faq.q8: Do the programmes allow for prayer times and meals?
faq.a8: Yes. We take prayer times into account when building the programme and stop at mosques along the route, and we point you to restaurants with halal options for lunch.
faq.a9: Yes — just tell us your child's age when you book. Baby and child seats are free of charge, but we do need to know in advance.
faq.q10: What currency are prices in, and how do I pay?
faq.a10: We quote in euro with the dollar equivalent alongside. Payment is in cash or by transfer during your trip; we do not ask for a deposit to hold a booking.
faq.a11: Yes. Cancellations made more than 24 hours before the programme starts are free of charge. If your plans change, a WhatsApp message is enough.
faq.q12: Do you serve cities outside Istanbul?
faq.a12: Yes. We are based in Istanbul but arrange transfers and tours to Bursa, Sapanca, Trabzon, Bodrum and other cities on request. On intercity journeys the same vehicle and driver stay with you.
faq.stillText: Write to us and we will come back the same day. Arabic, Turkish and English.
faq.q13: How far in advance should I book?
faq.a13: In the summer months and around Ramadan and the Eid holidays vehicles fill up early, and we suggest writing to us one or two weeks ahead for those dates. Otherwise a few days is enough, often the same day. We can only be certain once we see your dates — write to us and we will check availability straight away.
faq.q14: Do you operate during Ramadan and the Eid holidays?
faq.a14: Yes. During Ramadan the programme is built around iftar and suhoor: daytime stops are lightened and a place for iftar is arranged in advance. At Eid the city and roads get busier, so we move sightseeing earlier. Booking early matters in these periods.
faq.q15: What if my flight details change after booking?
faq.a15: Just send the new flight number and time on WhatsApp; there is no extra charge. The same goes for a change of hotel address. The earlier you tell us the better, but even at the last minute the vehicle and driver are redirected to the new information.
faq.q16: Can I change the itinerary during the trip?
faq.a16: Yes. Because the tours are private you can drop a stop, add one or reorder the day as you go — just tell your driver and guide. If the day runs longer or the route changes significantly we discuss the difference beforehand; nobody is caught out.
faq.q17: What languages are the tours conducted in?
faq.a17: Arabic, Turkish and English. City tours are accompanied by an Arabic-speaking guide; on some nature and shopping routes the Arabic-speaking driver takes on the guiding. We tell you plainly which applies to your programme before you book.
faq.q18: Is there wi-fi and water in the vehicle?
faq.a18: Water is free and cold in every vehicle, and there is charging on longer journeys. Internet is not fixed in every vehicle, though — tell us at booking and we arrange it for that day and confirm it in writing. If you need an unbroken connection along the way, buying your own eSIM or a tourist SIM is safer. The rear air conditioning runs separately and the windows are tinted.
faq.q19: Do you also book hotels and flight tickets?
faq.a19: Yes. Send us your dates, party size and budget and we will come back with two or three options and the total price for each; you approve the one you like and we make the booking. When we suggest a hotel we tell you in advance what the neighbourhood is like and how many minutes it is to the metro. We do not handle visa applications.
faq.q20: What does the TÜRSAB licence mean, and how do I verify it?
faq.a20: It means we operate as a travel agency under the supervision of the Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism; working without a licence is prohibited in Türkiye. Our licence number is 12539, and you can see for yourself that it is registered in our name through the agency search page on tursab.org.tr.

destinationsPage.introTitle: Choosing the city comes before choosing the hotel
destinationsPage.intro: Most guests pick the hotel first and only then find out where it is. But in Türkiye one city name can cover two hundred kilometres of coast: you might be half an hour from the airport or two and a half, your sea might be sand or pebble. These pages exist so you can make that decision first — they tell you what is in each region, how long it takes to get where, and which season actually works.
destinationsPage.askText: Send your dates and party size; we come back the same day with a fixed price and a day-by-day plan.
destinationsPage.compareTitle: The six cities side by side
destinationsPage.compareSubtitle: The real question on this page is usually not one city but the choice between two. The table answers that at a glance.
destinationsPage.combineTitle: How many cities you can combine
destinationsPage.combineText:
On a holiday of two weeks or less, at most two cities work. A third fits on paper but in practice costs two more days on the road and at the airport — a one-hour domestic flight takes five to six hours door to door.

The most popular shape is to start in Istanbul and move to a coastal city: four days in Istanbul, then Antalya or Bodrum. Bursa and Sapanca do not count as separate cities — both are day trips from Istanbul and enter the plan as a single day.

Trabzon works differently: the places worth seeing lie outside the city centre and the distances are long, so it is cramped in under five days and does not fit easily into the same week as another city.
